invented.sort: from the earliest invention to the most recent

rows.label: periodic table
rows.description: table systematically placing elements based on atomic number and recurrent properties
rows.hook: arranges every chemical element into rows and columns by atomic number

rows.label: photography
rows.description: art, science, and practice of creating durable images by recording light or other electromagnetic radiation
rows.hook: captures light on film or a sensor to freeze a moment into a picture

rows.label: World Wide Web
rows.description: global system of interlinked hypertext documents accessed via the Internet
rows.hook: lets people click links to jump between pages on the internet

rows.label: association football
rows.description: sport that is practiced between two teams of eleven players
rows.hook: is played with a round ball by two teams of eleven, with no hands allowed except for the goalkeeper

rows.label: web browser
rows.description: software application for retrieving, presenting, and traversing information resources on the World Wide Web
rows.hook: is the program you open to visit sites, such as Chrome or Firefox

rows.label: email
rows.description: electronic changing digital messages between a network
rows.hook: sends written messages instantly between inboxes, using an @ symbol in addresses

rows.label: Hypertext Transfer Protocol
rows.description: application-layer protocol for transferring web resources
rows.hook: is the set of rules that starts most website addresses in your browser

rows.label: basketball
rows.description: team sport played on a court with baskets on either end
rows.hook: has players dribble and shoot a ball through a hoop to score points

rows.label: HTML
rows.description: family of markup languages for displaying content in a web browser
rows.hook: is the code that structures the headings, links and images of a website

rows.label: Morse code
rows.description: communication code with signals representing letters, punctuation marks and numbers
rows.hook: sends messages using short and long beeps or flashes, famously spelling out SOS

rows.label: Esperanto
rows.description: international auxiliary language designed by L. L. Zamenhof

rows.label: volleyball
rows.description: team sport
rows.hook: has two teams hitting a ball over a high net without letting it touch the floor

rows.label: sudoku
rows.description: logic-based number-placement puzzle
rows.hook: challenges you to fill a nine-by-nine grid so no digit repeats in any row, column or box

rows.label: mobile phone
rows.description: portable device to make telephone calls using a radio link
rows.hook: lets people make calls from anywhere without a cord, first demonstrated by a Motorola engineer

rows.label: piano
rows.description: musical keyboard instrument
rows.hook: has black and white keys that strike strings with felt hammers

rows.label: Rubik's Cube
rows.description: 3-D combination puzzle with many different permutations
rows.hook: is a twisting puzzle of colored squares invented by a Hungarian architecture professor

rows.label: printing press
rows.description: device for evenly printing ink onto a print medium
rows.hook: let books be mass-produced, famously used for the Gutenberg Bible

rows.label: transistor
rows.description: a semiconductor device
rows.hook: is the tiny switch inside computer chips, with billions packed into each one

rows.label: airplane
rows.description: powered fixed-wing aircraft
rows.hook: carries passengers through the sky on fixed wings, first flown by two brothers from Ohio

rows.label: judo
rows.description: modern martial art, combat and Olympic/Paralympic sport
rows.hook: is a Japanese martial art of throws and holds whose name means the gentle way

rows.label: laser
rows.description: device which emits light via optical amplification
rows.hook: produces a narrow, intense beam of focused light used in pointers, surgery and cutting

rows.label: phonograph
rows.description: device for the analogue recording and playback of sound
rows.hook: plays sound recorded in grooves, first built by Thomas Edison

rows.label: diesel engine
rows.description: internal combustion engine with quality rotational frequency governing, internal mixture formation, lean air-fuel-ratio, diffusion flame and compression ignition
rows.hook: ignites fuel by squeezing air until it gets hot, powering trucks and trains

rows.label: transformer
rows.description: electrical device that transfers energy through electromagnetic induction from one circuit to another circuit

rows.label: saxophone
rows.description: single-reed woodwind instrument
rows.hook: is a curved brass woodwind with a single reed, loved in jazz

rows.label: microwave oven
rows.description: kitchen cooking appliance
rows.hook: heats leftovers fast, discovered when a radar engineer's candy bar melted

rows.label: telephone
rows.description: telecommunications device that permits two or more users to conduct a conversation
rows.hook: carries voices over wires, with its first patent famously going to Alexander Graham Bell

rows.label: hard disk
rows.description: data storage device
rows.hook: stores a computer's files on spinning magnetic platters inside a drive

rows.label: dynamite
rows.description: explosive preparation of stabilized nitroglycerin
rows.hook: is the explosive whose inventor funded the Nobel Prizes with his fortune

rows.label: computer mouse
rows.description: hand-held device used to move a pointer on a computer display
rows.hook: moves a pointer on screen when slid across a desk, first built from wood

rows.label: artificial satellite
rows.description: human-made object put into an orbit
rows.hook: circles Earth beaming signals, with Sputnik 1 the first to reach orbit

rows.label: bicycle
rows.description: pedal-driven two-wheel vehicle
rows.hook: moves on two wheels by pedaling, with the rider balancing

rows.label: tank
rows.description: armored fighting vehicle intended as a primary offensive weapon in front-line ground combat
rows.hook: is an armored vehicle on caterpillar tracks, first used in World War I

rows.label: pasteurization
rows.description: process in which certain foods are treated with mild heat in order to eliminate pathogens and extend shelf life
rows.hook: heats milk briefly to kill germs, and is named after a French chemist

rows.label: cotton gin
rows.description: machine that separates cotton fibers from seeds

rows.label: battery
rows.description: assembly of one or more electrochemical cells, used to provide devices with stored electrical energy
rows.hook: stores chemical energy to power flashlights, remotes and phones

rows.label: polio vaccine
rows.description: vaccine to prevent poliomyelitis
rows.hook: protected children from a disease that caused paralysis, first developed by Jonas Salk

rows.label: kaleidoscope
rows.description: cylinder with mirrors containing loose, colored objects such as beads or pebbles and bits of glass
rows.hook: shows shifting symmetrical patterns of colored glass when turned

rows.label: analytical engine
rows.description: proposed mechanical general-purpose computer, designed by Charles Babbage

rows.label: Ferris wheel
rows.description: amusement ride
rows.hook: is a giant rotating ride with passenger cabins, debuted at a Chicago world's fair

rows.label: smallpox vaccine
rows.description: first successful vaccine to be developed
rows.hook: protected people from a disease later eradicated, first tested using cowpox
